title: Preconditioned Implicit Midpoint Langevin Sampling for Non-Smooth Bayesian Imaging
claim: Neither preconditioning nor implicit integration alone suffices; only combining both yields fast, variance-accurate sampling.
layout: 2x2 color-coded table, rows integrator, columns preconditioning, winner cell highlighted
description: A compact 2x2 grid with column headers 'No preconditioning (M = I)' and 'Preconditioned (M ≈ ∇²f)', and row labels 'Explicit Euler' and 'Implicit midpoint'. Each cell holds a short verdict plus a method name and a variance-ratio (VR) value. The top row is shaded pink: 'slow-mixing' (ULA, VR = 0.24) and 'unstable' (P-ULA, VR → ∞). Bottom left is shaded peach: 'long transient' (IMLA, VR = 48.6). Bottom right is shaded green and set in bold: 'rapid relaxation' (P-IMLA, VR = 1.0246 ± 0.0001). The colors run from failure to success, so the eye goes first to the green cell. There are no images or arrows. The argument is made entirely by the layout and the color coding.
caption: The 2 × 2 landscape at a fixed simulation budget. Gaussian target with mean µ, precision H and κf = 4 × 107 (App. C.2). VR denotes the time-averaged normalised mean-square displacement from the target mean, d−1(X −µ)⊤H(X −µ), including the cold-start transient. It is not a stationary variance estimate. Both midpoint schemes are Gaussian-exact with exact solves; 98.7% of IMLA’s displayed 48.6 is transient mean error (App. D.5). Preconditioning makes that transient short at the reported budget.
abstract: We introduce P-IMLA, a preconditioned implicit-midpoint Langevin sampler for high-dimensional log-concave targets with non-smooth regularization. The obstruction is that the large steps enabled by matrix preconditioning are precisely where preconditioned Euler-Maruyama inflates stationary variance. Implicit midpoint removes this surplus via a Cayley-transform identity, making P-IMLA Gaussian-exact at any step size. Beyond Gaussians, whitening transfers the sharp IMLA contraction rate to $Îº_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and backward-error analysis gives drift-only rather than Euler-type diffusion bias under explicit smoothness assumptions. An $M$-norm Moreau envelope yields a proximal non-smooth variant with a three-term error budget. Controlled Gaussian and TV-regularized imaging experiments confirm the predicted separation: the unpreconditioned midpoint scheme retains long transients as $Îº_f$ grows, whereas P-IMLA remains $Îº_{\mathrm{eff}}$-governed and near variance-exact.
